findings_qualitative.value: Only a receding molecular outflow component is detected, extending to ~10 kpc, ~3 times the ionized wind size, with a positive velocity gradient

evidence.quote: extends for at least $\sim$10 kpc from the nuclear region, about three times the projected size of the ionized wind

claims.hypothesis: Is there a molecular outflow in zC400528 and how large is it?
claims.experiment: Disk-model subtraction of CO(3-2) cube and channel maps
claims.result: Red wing at +300 to +500 km/s extending ~10 kpc, 3.36e9 Msun
claims.finding: A powerful, asymmetric molecular outflow is detected

evidence.quote: We detect a powerful molecular outflow that shows a positive velocity gradient

claims.hypothesis: Which phase dominates the outflow mass and energetics?
claims.experiment: Compare molecular to literature ionized outflow

evidence.quote: we find that the mass and energetics of the outflow are dominated by the molecular phase

claims.hypothesis: Can the outflow quench star formation?
claims.result: Outflow depletion time ~2x shorter than SF depletion
claims.finding: Outflow is one of the main quenching engines

evidence.quote: This suggests that the nuclear outflow is one of the main quenching engines at work in the observed suppression of the central star-formation activity in zC400528.

why_this_method.value: High spatial resolution and S/N allow channel-by-channel disk subtraction instead of two-Gaussian decomposition, which gives upper limits

evidence.quote: Given that we have sufficient spatial resolution and signal-to-noise (S/N) in our ALMA CO(3-2) data, here we try a different strategy
